newsitem.title: USA: Stratosphere debt falls, Chapter 11 nears.
newsitem.headline: Stratosphere debt falls, Chapter 11 nears.

text.p: Bids for Stratosphere Corp debt were lower in thin markets on Tuesday after the company said it is headed for bankruptcy, traders said.

Stratosphere's $203 million 14-1/4 percent first mortgage notes were bid down about 10 points to 85, with no offers seen immediately after the news, traders said. One big shop in New York indicated a less dramatic drop for the notes to a 90 bid, 95 offer market, however.
The Las Vegas hotel and casino said it failed make a $14.5 million interest payment on November 15 and that it does not expect to do so before the end of a 30-day grace period.
Wedelstaedt said reaction to an actual bankruptcy filing will be contingent on the success of current bondholder negotiations, or lack thereof.

"If they file for bankruptcy with no consensual plan with bondholders they market may again be disappointed because people have predicated their getting that plan in place," she said. "If not, this could drag out and it would suggest they still need to find a new source of cash to come in."
Stratosphere has confirmed it is seeking additional financing and a debt restructuring. Construction of a second hotel tower was suspended in August because of a cash shortfall, Stratosphere said.

For all its shortcomings, Wedelstaedt noted the company has done an extraordinarily good job with disclosure. The company in August said it questioned whether it could continue as a going concern if it is unable to amend the terms of the outstanding notes.

Standard & Poor's rating agency on Tuesday slashed its rating on the notes to single-D from CC, citing the missed payment and probable bankruptcy. Moody's Investors Service cut the notes to Caa from B2 on August 19.

The company said it is "highly likely" that current talks with creditors will involve a bankrupcy filing part of a restructuring plan. At the same time, it said a bankruptcy filing would not adversely affect daily operations.

Barbara Wedelstaedt, vice president at KDP Investment Advisors Inc, said the debt was far overvalued and a back-up was imminent. But it took Tuesday's news to put a halt to a surprising upward trend seen over the past week, she said.
"People may have expected that because there was no leakage of news lately that there was a possibility negotiations were going strongly," Wedelstaedt said.

One view that suggested bondholders would receive principal plus interest in a restructuring may have been behind the recent rise in the notes, she said. But even if that were true, she contended the bonds are still not worth more than 76 cents on the dollar.

"That (view) assumes a valuation higher than $215 million and we question that for a company that's not generating positive cash flow," she said, adding that Stratosphere still needs more capital to complete its second hotel tower.
